title: Tilly's Tiny Tart Worry
markdown:
Tilly the teddy bear was having a super-duper, perfectly splendid morning. The sun was like a warm, fuzzy blanket draped over the whole world, making everything sparkle and shine like a million tiny disco balls. The flowers in their little meadow weren’t just any flowers; they were giggling with sunshine yellow and daisy white, their petals doing a happy dance in the softest breeze. Right beside Tilly sat Moss the mouse, her bestest, bravest friend. He twitched his little nose, sniffing the air that smelled like sweet, green grass and warm, sleepy earth. Tilly sat very still, her button eyes, round and brown like two yummy chocolate drops, looking out at the sunny world. She was a very thoughtful bear, always thinking about her friends. But sometimes, just sometimes, when no one was looking, a tiny, wiggly worry would flutter in her tummy about things. Like, what if there wasn't quite enough of something special? It was a very quiet worry, like a little mouse tiptoeing through a quiet room.

"Oh, Tilly!" squeaked Moss, doing a little hop so high his whiskers tickled the sky. "It's such a perfect day for a picnic! A super-duper, tremendously terrific picnic!"

Tilly nodded, her fluffy ears, soft as dandelion fluff, bobbing happily. "It really is, Moss. The sun is just right for munching tasty treats. And guess what? I've got just the thing!" From behind a big, smooth pebble, the kind that feels lovely and cool on your paws, Tilly carefully brought out a tiny, round jam tart. And oh my goodness, it was the most perfect jam tart you ever did see. It was like a little golden sun, and peeking out from under its wonderfully flaky crust was a glistening, ruby-red jam filling that looked like a tiny, happy jewel.

"Ooh! A jam tart!" Moss chirped, his whiskers wiggling so fast they looked like they were trying to escape and do a jig. "Just one? Oh boy oh boy oh boy!"

"Just one," Tilly said, her voice a little quieter than a whisper, like a secret shared between friends. "And it’s the very last one from Mrs. Higgins's famous bakery. She makes the best jam tarts in the whole wide world, you know!" A little flutter, like a tiny butterfly trying to get out of a jam jar, started in Tilly's tummy. What if it wasn't enough for two of them? What if Moss took a bigger bite than her? What if it all disappeared too fast, like a balloon floating away into the blue sky? *Oh dear, oh dear,* she thought, her button eyes looking a little less twinkly. *What if there isn't enough? This is a big worry for such a tiny tart!*

"Hooray for the last jam tart!" Moss announced, bouncing with sheer joy. "Let's take it to the big, blue picnic blanket! It’s waiting for us, I just know it!"

Tilly clutched the tart, her paws feeling a little clammy. The big, blue picnic blanket wasn't just next door; it was a little way across the meadow, past the field of wobbly dandelions and the busy path where all the ladybugs liked to have their meetings. This was new territory for a picnic with only one, precious tart. Tilly's secret worry, her little tummy gremlin, was this: she was always afraid there wouldn't be enough of the good things to go around.

"Okay," Tilly said, trying to sound as brave as a lion, even though she felt more like a tiny field mouse. "Let's go. But we have to be super, super careful." But if they didn't take the tart now, the sun might go down, and then no picnic at all! And Mrs. Higgins's bakery would be closed forever and ever and ever! So, Tilly the teddy bear and Moss the little mouse set off. Tilly held the tart very, very carefully in her paws, cradling it like a tiny baby. She tried not to wobble too much, but the grass tickled her feet and her tummy felt like it was doing a little dance. The sun felt warm and pleasant on her fur, like a gentle hug. But then, a little puff of wind, whoosh! it blew past them, faster than a speedy snail. It carried the scent of dry grass and tickled Tilly's fur with unseen fingers, making a lonely dandelion seed spin like a tiny dancer. "Watch out, Tilly!" squeaked Moss, his little voice a bit higher than usual. Tilly hugged the tart tighter, her furry arms squeezing it so much she thought she heard a tiny squeak from the crust. The puff of wind was like a tiny, playful breeze, but it made Tilly’s worry flutter more, like those dandelion seeds taking flight. What if the wind got stronger? What if it blew their precious tart away, far, far away to a land of no jam?

Then, scritch-scratch-scurry! A busy little beetle, with a shell that shone like a polished button, zipped right across their path. Moss jumped so high he almost tumbled over, and Tilly let out a tiny, surprised sigh that ruffled her fur. The beetle was gone in a flash, a streak of brown disappearing into the green. But Tilly’s tummy fluttered again, this time like a whole swarm of butterflies. It felt like a lot of excitement, a lot of sudden movements, for just one little tart that needed to be kept perfectly safe. She kept picturing it getting smaller and smaller, not from eating, but from all the bumpy excitement. *Oh dear, oh dear,* she thought, her paws getting a little sweaty. *This journey is quite bumpy and full of surprises! What if my tummy worry is right?*

Finally, after what felt like a whole adventure in itself, they reached the big, blue picnic blanket. It was spread out under a leafy green tree, looking ever so inviting, like a big, soft cloud waiting for them. Tilly carefully, oh so carefully, placed the tiny jam tart right in the middle of the vast blue expanse. But oh dear! On the big, blue blanket, the tart looked really, really tiny. It looked like a speck of glitter on a giant blue blanket! Maybe even smaller! Approximately one crumb small! Tilly’s tummy did a big flip. It was so small! She quickly nudged it closer to her, thinking, 'Maybe if I just take a little nibble... just a teeny, tiny one... no one will know...' but then she saw Moss's happy face and her paws felt all tingly and wrong.

Tilly took a deep breath. Not a little puff of air, oh no. A big, slow, teddy bear breath, the kind that fills up your whole fluffy body. She looked at Moss’s happy, expectant face. She remembered how much fun they had walking together, even with the wobbly dandelions and the speedy beetles. She remembered the sunshine and the sweet smell of the grass. She picked up the tart, her paws a little hesitant. She pictured herself taking the whole tart, gobbling it up, and then Moss looking a bit sad, his little whiskers drooping. *No,* she decided, her button eyes firming up. *That’s not the best thing. Not at all.* With a gentle paw, she carefully, lovingly, pushed the tart towards Moss. "Moss," she said, her voice soft but clear, and full of a new kind of bravery. "Shall we share?" Oh! Oh! This is the best part! Moss’s eyes lit up like two tiny stars. "Yes, please, Tilly! I’d love to share!"

Tilly nudged the tart closer. She hesitated, watching the tart roll slightly. The thought of not having any of that sweet, ruby jam, not even a tiny bite, made her tummy feel like it was full of cold pebbles. She could almost hear the crunch of the crust in her imagination, a sound that now belonged to Moss. She knew this was giving up the one thing she'd wanted. It was a big, big thing to give away. Her paws felt heavy, and a little bit of her wanted to snatch it back, but she didn't. She watched Moss take a small bite, and his eyes sparkled. That was her sacrifice. Her tart. For Moss. And as they sat on the big blue blanket, with only a few delightful crumbs left, Tilly the teddy bear felt like the luckiest, happiest bear in the whole entire world. She didn't even feel that little worry anymore. Not even a teeny, tiny bit. It had vanished like a bad dream when you wake up to a sunny morning. Her tummy felt warm and full of a happy, glowy feeling, like she’d swallowed a tiny, happy sunbeam. Sharing the tiny jam tart had made it feel like the biggest, most wonderful treat in the whole wide meadow. She realised that having enough wasn't always about how much there was, but about how you enjoyed it with a friend.

Tilly and Moss, with only a few happy crumbs left on the blanket, looked at each other and giggled. The sun was still warm, the blanket was still blue, and the meadow was still full of giggling flowers. Everything was just as it had been before, but also different. They hadn't gone far, just across the meadow, but they had come back with something much more valuable than a whole tart. They had come back with the happy feeling of sharing.

Tilly the teddy bear stretched out on the soft blue blanket. A little breeze rustled the leaves of the tree above them. It was a gentle breeze, not a whooshing, worry-making wind at all. A little dandelion seed, looking like a tiny white parachute, floated past. Tilly watched it go. Before, the thought of that seed blowing near their precious tart would have sent a little shiver of worry down her spine. But now? Now she just smiled. The seed danced in the air, free and happy. Just like her heart. The worry about not having enough had gone, replaced by the happy warmth of sharing with her best friend. And that, she knew, was more than enough. It was just perfect.
characters: Tilly the teddy bear, Moss the little mouse
